content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge resolves a challenged link by assessing the chapter-bound witnesses alongside the conceded application and word-count evidence.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' can mean the judge must weigh the cumulative support of each side's whole chain rather than tally isolated verses; the judge's summary of chapter bounds, Matthew 1:23, and Joel 1:8 could be read either as a cumulative chain assessment or as an isolated verse tally.","why":"The judge treats the challenger's chapter bounds as real and balances them against the conceded application and word-count evidence rather than rejecting them because no single verse states the contrary."}
